text.p: Russia's upper house of parliament, dissatisfied with the government's work, urged President Boris Yeltsin on Tuesday to improve radically the cabinet's efficiency.

"The government action is inadequate to the situation in the country and the society," a Federation Council resolution said after Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Tuesday promised to pay all wage and pensions arrears soon.
"The Federation Council asks the president to immediately carry out radical measures to provide more efficient work of the government in the field of social-economic development," said the document.
Yeltsin is recovering after a quintuple heart bypass operation in a country residence near Moscow.
Chernomyrdin, addressing the upper house of parliament on Tuesday, pledged to pay wage arrears in December and pensions in the first two months of 1997.

But he also told Russian regional administration leaders, who sit in the Federation Council, that budget subsidies to the regions would be only 63.3 percent of planned levels this year because the regions themselves owe a lot of money to the government.
Chernomyrdin angered the upper house last week by ignoring a plea to address it, but held out an olive branch on Monday, saying he would meet them.
The prime minister also faces a contentious vote on the 1997 budget in the lower house, the State Duma, scheduled for Sunday.
Chernomyrdin said he hoped the Duma would pass the budget plan in the first reading. He said the main budget targets, a 3.5-percent budget deficit and 11-12 percent inflation, could not be changed.
"If we make them higher, the capital would stay in the banking sector, and all (capital) growth would be eaten up by government securities," Chernomyrdin said.
If deputies fail to approve a new budget by the end of the year Russia will have to adopt interim budgets or repeat the 1996 budget.
